newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end down but off lows.

text.p: French shares clambered back off the day's lows but closed slightly softer on Thursday.
A bigger than expected rise 0.8 percent rise in U.S. February retail sales sent bond and share prices lower, but the CAC index narrowed the loss as a few blue-chip rises gave support.
Traders said there was caution about a potential tightening of U.S. interest rates on March 25 and Friday's release of U.S. producer prices data should hold the market's gaze.
The CAC-40 index closed down 9.60 points or 0.36 percent at 2,632.10. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 24.5 at 2,632 from Wednesday's close.
Banking blue-chip BNP bounced back, rising 3.7 percent to 272, on short covering after heavy falls earlier this week on rumours that insurer Axa-UAP would lighten its holding.
Cement company Lafarge up 2.8 percent at 382.4, gave a bullish presentation yesterday which led several brokers to upgrade recommendations and earnings forecasts.
Assurances Generale de France erases earlier weakness, ends up 1.9 percent at 214.5. The insurer posted 1996 net attributable profit up 42 percent at 1.54 billion francs after the close.
